standards.title: Customs IT Security & Data Residency Standard
standards.description: Security and data-residency requirements for every system that processes customs data, including systems supplied and maintained by vendors. Issued by the General Customs Directorate, Information Security Office (v3.1, March 2026).

rules.text: All customs data (scan images, metadata, analyst annotations, logs and backups) shall be stored and processed only within the national territory.
Systems shall run on Directorate infrastructure; no component may depend on a public cloud service for operation, licensing, telemetry or updates.
Users shall authenticate through the Directorate's Active Directory over LDAPS, with role-based access control mapped to job functions.
Multi-factor authentication is required for all administrative accounts and for any remote access.
Local accounts shall enforce passwords of at least 12 characters and lock after 5 failed attempts; interactive sessions shall lock after 15 minutes of inactivity.
Tamper-evident audit logs of all user and administrator actions shall be retained for 5 years and forwarded in real time to the Directorate's SIEM using syslog or CEF.
Data shall be encrypted at rest with AES-256 and in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher, using certificates issued by the Directorate's PKI.
In addition to routine patch releases, critical vulnerabilities shall be remediated within 14 days and high-severity vulnerabilities within 30 days of disclosure, throughout warranty and maintenance.
An independent penetration test shall be performed before go-live; all critical and high findings shall be closed before acceptance.
Vendor remote access is allowed only through the Directorate's VPN, approved per session, with the full session recorded.

Backups shall be taken daily, encrypted, and stored on-premise at a second site, with a recovery point objective of 24 hours or better and a recovery time objective of 8 hours or better for image management platforms.
Vendor staff with administrative access shall pass the Directorate's security vetting and sign a confidentiality undertaking before access is granted.
A Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) shall be delivered for all supplied software and updated with every release.
Architecture, data-flow and hardening documentation shall be delivered before the Site Acceptance Test.

standards.title: Port Equipment Safety & Environmental Standard
standards.description: Health, safety and environmental requirements for equipment installed and operated in the port, including radiation-emitting inspection systems. Issued by the NGPA Health, Safety & Environment Department (v2.0, January 2026).

rules.text: No radiation-emitting equipment may be operated before it is licensed by the national radiation regulator.
The annual dose at the boundary of any controlled area shall not exceed 1 mSv (public limit); occupational exposure shall be kept as low as reasonably achievable (ALARA).
Occupied vehicle cabs shall never be exposed to the primary high-energy beam; any cab scanning shall use a low-dose mode delivering 0.25 µSv or less per pass.
Controlled areas shall be marked with bilingual (Arabic and English) radiation warning signs, beam-on warning lights and audible alarms.
Emergency stop buttons, interlocked with the radiation source, shall be reachable within 10 metres from any point inside the controlled area.
The supplier shall provide personal dosimeters for operators during the first 12 months of operation and train all operators in radiation protection.
Outdoor equipment shall be rated for continuous operation from 0 °C to +50 °C and up to 95% relative humidity in a saline atmosphere, with electronics enclosures of at least IP54.
Structural steel shall be protected for corrosivity category C5-M (ISO 12944) with a design durability of at least 15 years.
Noise from equipment, including HVAC units and generators, shall not exceed 70 dB(A) at 1 metre from operator cabins.
Hazardous waste (oils, batteries, lead shielding off-cuts and decommissioned sources) shall be removed by the supplier through licensed contractors, with disposal certificates.
Before civil works start, method statements and risk assessments shall be approved by the HSE Department, and the supplier shall keep a full-time HSE officer on site.
Operator cabins and electrical rooms shall have fire detection; server and electrical rooms shall have clean-agent fire suppression.

standards.title: Procurement Commercial & Contract Terms Standard
standards.description: Commercial, financial-security and contractual rules that apply to every NGPA procurement. Issued by the NGPA Procurement Directorate (v7.0, July 2025).

rules.text: Bid securities, advance payment guarantees and performance securities shall be issued or confirmed by a bank licensed in the State.
Prices shall be quoted in the currency stated in the tender documents; capital prices are firm unless the contract provides otherwise.
Advance payments are made only against an advance payment guarantee of equal value.
Apart from the advance payment, no milestone payment may exceed the value of the work delivered or accepted at that milestone.
A performance security of at least 10% of the contract price, valid until 28 days after final acceptance, is required.
Bidders shall disclose every subcontractor performing more than 10% of the contract value and any conflict of interest.
The supplier's own general terms and conditions do not apply to Authority contracts.
Bidders claiming local value added shall provide a breakdown certified by an independent auditor.
Maintenance, spare-part and support prices for the maintenance period shall be quoted per year; any annual escalation shall not exceed the cap stated in the tender documents.
Bidders shall sign the Authority's integrity pledge; any breach leads to disqualification and may lead to debarment.
Invoices shall be in English, quote the tender reference, follow the line items of the price schedule and show the supplier's tax registration number.
Contracts are governed by the laws of the State, with arbitration seated in the capital.

projects.name: Cargo X-Ray Inspection Systems — Port of Al-Noor (sample)
projects.description: Supply, installation, commissioning and 5-year maintenance of four high-energy drive-through cargo X-ray inspection systems (T1 Gate A, T1 Gate B, T2 and one relocatable unit) with a central image analysis centre. Tender NGPA/T/2026/014.

projects.name: Port Community System — Web Platform and Integration (sample)
projects.description: Web portal, messaging hub and integrations (TOS, customs, Maritime Single Window, ERP) for the Port of Al-Noor community, with a truck appointment system and 3 years of support. Tender NGPA/T/2026/021.
